sections.title: Join Elimination — When the Planner Skips the Join

blocks.md: Join elimination = free performance. If child has FK to parent PK, and you only select parent PK/FK columns, planner skips parent table entirely. The FK IS the data.

blocks.label: join elimination example
blocks.code:
-- Schema: employees.dept_id → departments.id (FK)
-- Query only needs dept_id (already in employees!)
SELECT dept_id FROM employees;
-- Planner: no join needed! Seq Scan on employees only.

-- But adding department name kills elimination
SELECT e.dept_id, d.name
FROM employees e
JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;
-- Now join required

-- LEFT JOIN also blocks elimination (might need NULL check)
SELECT e.dept_id FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON ...;
blocks.pg:
-- Join elimination works for INNER JOIN on FK→PK
-- Requires: FK not nullable, only PK/FK columns from parent
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0.16+: Join elimination supported
-- Similar rules: FK→PK, only PK columns from parent
blocks.py-pandas: # No planner; just don't merge if you don't need columns

blocks.title: Join Eliminated — Only Child Table Scanned

blocks.md: Zero join cost. Planner sees dept_id already in employees (FK). No need to touch departments table. Join elimination = zero-cost optimization for star schemas.

items.explain: FK not nullable + only PK columns from parent + INNER JOIN = safe elimination.

items.q: SELECT d.name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON ... — eliminated?
items.explain: Need d.name (non-PK) from parent → join required. Elimination only when parent columns = PK/FK.

sections.title: Predicate Pushdown — Filter Early, Join Less

blocks.label: predicate pushdown
blocks.code:
-- View with filter
CREATE VIEW active_employees AS
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE status = 'active';

-- Query with additional filter
SELECT * FROM active_employees WHERE dept_id = 3;
-- Planner pushes dept_id=3 INTO view scan
-- Single scan: status='active' AND dept_id=3

-- CTE pushdown
WITH active AS (SELECT * FROM employees WHERE status = 'active')
SELECT * FROM active WHERE dept_id = 3;
-- Same pushdown

-- Subquery pushdown
SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM employees WHERE status = 'active') e
WHERE dept_id = 3;
-- Pushdown works
blocks.pg:
-- Pushdown automatic in PostgreSQL
-- Can be blocked by: VOLATILE functions, LIMIT/OFFSET in subquery, set operations
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL 8.0+: predicate pushdown improved
-- Derived table pushdown (merged)
blocks.py-pandas:
# Manual pushdown: filter first, then merge
active = employees[employees['status'] == 'active']
result = active[active['dept_id'] == 3]

blocks.md: Pushdown blockers: VOLATILE functions (random(), now()), LIMIT/OFFSET in subquery, UNION/EXCEPT, window functions in subquery, set operations. Use CTEs carefully.

items.q: Predicate pushdown shrinks the rows entering a join by moving the filter:
options: From outer query INTO inner subquery/CTE
items.explain: Pushing the predicate into the inner subquery/CTE filters rows at the source, so fewer rows enter the join — cheaper probe/build.

items.q: A LIMIT inside a CTE is a pushdown boundary because:
items.explain: In PostgreSQL, CTEs are optimization fences (materialized). LIMIT inside CTE prevents pushdown.

sections.title: Partition-Wise Join — Parallel Join at Scale

blocks.label: partition-wise join
blocks.pg:
-- Partition-wise join (PostgreSQL 11+)
-- Requires: same partition key, same partition bounds
blocks.mysql:
-- MySQL: no native partition-wise join
-- Partition pruning only
blocks.py-pandas:
# Manual partition-wise: groupby partition key, join per group
for key, group in events.groupby('event_month'):
    orders_m = orders[orders['month'] == key]
    merged = group.merge(orders_m, on='user_id')

blocks.md: Each partition joins independently → massive parallelism. 12 monthly partitions = 12 parallel joins. Linear scale-out for time-series data. enable_partitionwise_aggregate pushes GROUP BY into partitions too.

options: Same partition key on both tables
items.explain: Both tables must be partitioned identically on the join key. Each partition pair joins independently.
Aggregate in each partition, then combine. Massive parallel GROUP BY.
